about.p1: I'm Marcela Gotta, a software engineer in Madrid. I've spent 12 years building software: I started full-stack, fell in love with frontend and ended up leading teams and architecture.
about.p2: Since 2019 I've been at Sngular, where I'm Head Frontend Developer and part of the team that runs the frontend chapter: training, technical follow-up for each person, and technical interviews. I've led product teams for large companies in banking, fashion, energy and sustainability.
about.p3: I believe AI is the most powerful tool we've had, as long as people stay on the side that steers it. My own work tries to build that part, in the open: Kimen, Jezero and Orbit. And a method for working with agents without losing quality: GDD.
about.p4: I live in Madrid with a small zoo. I love physics, video games, writing and turning odd ideas into things that work.

kimen.desc: The component base for generative interfaces: Web Components that work in any framework, and that agents can read and use through a clear contract.
bullets: 29 ki-* components with no framework dependency, plus wrappers for React, Vue and Angular.
Guarded catalog: an agent can only render declared components and actions; anything unknown is rejected.
Adapters for A2UI and MCP Apps.
Accessibility as a hard gate: zero axe violations in CI and a WCAG 2.2 AA target. Under 10 KB per component.

jezero.sub: The shared memory of your agents' work.
jezero.desc: Your agents forget. Jezero gathers their sessions, summarises them and lets any agent ask what was decided, what failed or which command worked, even if another agent did it weeks ago.
bullets: Incremental, read-only connectors for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity and Paperclip.
Each session is summarised into “atoms”: decisions, reasons, fixes, exact errors, commands, data and risks.
A single SQLite file with full-text search: milliseconds, no GPU.
A read-only MCP server: every agent can query, none can write. Secrets are redacted before saving.
jezero.note: the Martian crater that used to be a lake. Its sediments keep what happened, and that is where Perseverance sets samples aside to be collected later.

orbit.desc: A Mac app that gives your assistant a place in your day: it records and transcribes your meetings, writes the notes and lets you talk to the agent of your choice.
bullets: Bring your own agent: through an API gateway or with your Claude or Codex session.
Includes its own self-hosted hub: you decide where your meetings live.

method.name: GDD
method.sub: Your agent says “done.” The gate checks if it's true.
method.desc: My method for building quality products with AI agents without supervising them step by step. Before the agent starts, you decide what it has to prove: those are the gates. The more that can go wrong, the stricter they are, and whatever slips through becomes a new gate.
bullets: It passes with facts, not words: tests, linters, a reviewer or your approval.
The agent never touches the checks that judge it.
Risk decides how much is on you: on green, nothing; on red, you approve where it matters.
Every change is owned by its author: AI never answers for you.
method.status: v0.6, a draft for review. No data of its own yet; its engine, T-minus, is in development.
